claims.text: Adding approximately 1 atomic % yttrium to a refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its radiation tolerance.
The yttrium addition will preserve the alloy's mechanical integrity.
The yttrium addition will preserve engineering practicality.
Yttrium will promote formation of yttrium-rich nanoscale oxide dispersions at grain boundaries and within the matrix.
Yttrium segregates to grain boundaries in the refractory high-entropy alloy.
Segregated yttrium forms stable nano-oxides when exposed to trace oxygen or controlled oxidation during processing.
Yttrium-rich oxide dispersoids act as sinks for radiation-induced vacancies and interstitials.
Defect trapping by the oxide dispersoids reduces radiation-induced defect accumulation.
Reduced defect accumulation minimizes radiation-induced swelling.
Reduced defect accumulation mitigates radiation-induced embrittlement.
The oxide dispersions will not significantly disrupt the alloy's bulk mechanical properties.
The yttrium-doped alloy will exhibit less radiation-induced swelling than the unmodified alloy under identical irradiation conditions.
The yttrium-doped alloy will retain more tensile strength after irradiation than the unmodified alloy.
Microstructural analysis of the yttrium-doped alloy will reveal well-dispersed nano-oxides.
Temperatures of 600–900°C are favorable for formation and stability of the proposed yttrium-rich oxides under simulated plasma-facing irradiation.
Temperatures or radiation fluxes outside the proposed operating range may compromise oxide formation or stability and limit the intervention's effectiveness.
